fixes.explanation: Right, baker. Moses says the tablets were “…inscribed by the finger of God with the exact words that the LORD spoke to you out of the fire on the mountain…” Think about that. The same words the people heard out of the fire were now written down by God Himself. Nobody had to guess what He said, because they could read it.

Nothing in the text has Moses lifting them up, friend. He says he took the two tablets and threw them out of his hands, shattering them before the people's eyes. That's not a victory pose. I think that moment hurt, because he'd just carried those tablets down the mountain. The people watched it happen.

Close on the material, friend, but an altar isn't what the LORD asks for here. He tells Moses to chisel out two stone tablets, then adds an ark of wood (Deuteronomy 10:1). No altar is named in these verses. Moses is chiseling and building, and I'd be sore by lunchtime.

Gold is a nice thought, friend, but the LORD doesn't mention it here. Moses is told to chisel out two stone tablets and make an ark of wood (Deuteronomy 10:1). Later Moses says he made it of acacia wood. That's a chisel job and a woodworking job, and I'd need a nap after both.

No spies come up in this part, friend. Moses says the LORD your God “…goes across ahead of you as a consuming fire…” Spies go in first to see how scary things look. Here the LORD Himself is already out front, so Israel doesn't need anyone sneaking ahead to check the giants. That's one scouting trip I'd happily cancel.

Seven is a good guess, friend, but Moses doesn't say it here. He says he stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, and that he ate no bread and drank no water. That's a long time up there with the LORD. The tablets of the covenant came at the end of that stretch.

Horeb doesn't come up in this instruction, friend. The LORD tells Moses to continue his journey ahead of the people, so they may enter and possess the land He swore to their fathers. Moses was just at the mountain, and the LORD sends him forward. The LORD doesn't want a U-turn. Not one.
